title: Nine Rows of Frost
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：cabbage　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cabbage 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my mother was sent to lift ① a cabbage she could not carry, and she said the carrying was the whole of the lesson. The ② cabbage, meaning the head and not the row, was nine pounds and was cut by whoever came last; a cabbage, she said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cabbage in that field had the same frost, and the ④ cabbage at the end, meaning the one the gardener kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever lifted properly. A cabbage, my grandmother said, is nine parts water and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the water is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cabbage was the whole of the winter, meaning the store it stood for and not the head. The ⑥ cabbage, meaning the store and not any of that, is the only thing in a village that everybody boils and nobody questions; a cabbage, he said, is either something you lift or the only word that means both a head and a store. She said the store is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ cabbage had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the frost. The ⑧ cabbage of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine rows and eleven years of lifting; a cabbage, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cabbage I remember is the one at the end, which was stored in 1971 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ cabbage, my grandmother said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being boiled; every cabbage, she said, is a store that has agreed to look like a head. She said the store was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 卷心菜；洋白菜
B. n. 卷心菜（指那棵菜本身，与整畦相对）
C. 固定搭配：lift a cabbage 把一棵卷心菜从地里起出来
D. n. 卷心菜（指地里每一棵）
E. n. 卷心菜（指末尾那一棵）
F. n. 卷心菜（抽象：它所代表的储备）
G. n. 那份储备（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a cabbage she could not carry
The cabbage, meaning the head and not the row
cabbage was the whole of the winter
the cabbage had become a photograph in a report
The cabbage of the whole thing
A cabbage, my grandmother said in 1975

answers.why: lift a cabbage 意为“把一棵卷心菜从地里起出来”，1948 年母亲被派去起一棵她搬不动的卷心菜。
cabbage 意为“卷心菜”，指那棵菜本身而不是整畦，重九磅，由最后走的人砍下。
cabbage 指地里每一棵卷心菜，每一棵都是同样的霜。
cabbage 指末尾那一棵（园丁留的那一棵），是唯一有人认真起出来的。
cabbage 意为“卷心菜”，抽象指它所代表的储备，父亲说 cabbage 就是那个冬天的全部。
cabbage 为抽象用法，指那份储备本身，是村子里人人都煮、却没人质疑的东西。
cabbage 意为“卷心菜、洋白菜”，到 1966 年这棵 cabbage 成了报告里的一张照片。
cabbage 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九畦菜和十一年的起菜。
cabbage 意为“卷心菜”，我记得的是末尾那一棵，1971 年入窖，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
cabbage 为抽象总称，祖母说卷心菜是唯一会因为被煮进锅里而变好的东西。
